While this was a significant event, it was not the largest earthquake in Alaska in 2023; a magnitude 7.2 earthquake occurred on July 16 in the Alaska Peninsula region. [1, 4, 6] The event, which had been announced on October 16, 2023, was designed to test the base's mass notification systems, including the public address system. [2, 3] The explicit purpose of the exercise was to ensure that all Marine Corps personnel and their families at the installation are prepared to react appropriately in the event of a significant earthquake. [5] <3> A magnitude 2.9 earthquake, reviewed by a seismologist, occurred 7 km SSW of Chandler, Oklahoma, on October 14, 2023. [5, 7, 12] This process can increase fluid pressure on ancient, buried faults, reactivating them and causing earthquakes. [1] The tour made stops in Sacramento, San Francisco, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Los Angeles, Riverside, and concluded in San Diego on the official Great California ShakeOut Day. [1] <5> Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin announced the results of a seven-month trial in China where an AI algorithm they developed successfully predicted 70% of earthquakes. [5] The AI, trained on five years of seismic data, provided weekly forecasts and correctly predicted 14 earthquakes a week in advance, within approximately 200 miles of the actual location and at nearly the correct magnitude. [5, 7] During the trial, the AI missed one earthquake and issued eight false warnings. [5, 6] The UT-developed AI, led by seismologist Yangkang Chen, won first place out of 600 entries in an international competition held in China. [5, 11] The achievement is considered a significant milestone in AI-driven earthquake forecasting, though researchers note it has not yet been tested in other locations. [5, 8] <6> Millions of people across the United States and worldwide participated in the Great ShakeOut, an annual earthquake preparedness drill held on October 19, 2023. The drill is observed annually on the third Thursday of October. At 10:19 a.m. local time, participants practiced the "Drop, Cover, and Hold On" safety procedure to raise awareness and encourage individuals, schools, and organizations to develop and test their emergency plans for surviving and recovering from an earthquake. In the U.S. alone, over 17.5 million people were expected to participate. <7> A magnitude 5.0 earthquake occurred in a rural area of Shasta County, northeast of Redding, California, on Friday, September 8, 2023, at approximately 10:24 a.m. Pacific Time. The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) reported the quake's depth to be about 9 miles. The shaking was felt by residents in nearby communities, including Redding, Burney, and Susanville. People as far north as Klamath Falls, Oregon, and as far south as Chico also reported feeling the tremor. The initial quake was followed by aftershocks, including a magnitude 4.4 event around 2:25 p.m. the same day. While widely felt, there were no immediate reports of significant damage or injuries. The ShakeAlert earthquake warning system was activated as a result of the event. <8> A preliminary magnitude 3.9 aftershock struck near Ojai, California, on August 22, 2023. This tremor was one of several aftershocks that followed a larger 5.1-magnitude earthquake, which had occurred in the same area two days earlier on Sunday, August 20, 2023. <9> A magnitude 5.1 earthquake struck Southern California on August 20, 2023, at 2:41 p.m. PDT, with its epicenter located about 4 miles southeast of Ojai in Ventura County. The quake, which occurred on the Sisar fault system at a shallow depth, was preceded by a smaller foreshock sequence and followed by numerous aftershocks. Shaking was widely felt across the region, from Santa Barbara to San Diego and as far as Fresno. The event coincided with the arrival of Tropical Storm Hilary, the first tropical storm to hit the area since 1939, prompting the term 'hurriquake' to trend on social media platforms. Seismologists and scientists confirmed the two natural events were unrelated. There were no reports of significant structural damage or serious injuries. Reported damage was minor, including a downed power line, a damaged cellphone tower, broken bottles in stores, and a few fallen art pieces in Ojai. <10> A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck off the coast of the Alaska Peninsula on July 15, 2023, at 10:48 PM local time (July 16, 2023 UTC). The quake, which occurred at a depth of about 20-32.6 km, was a late aftershock of the magnitude 7.8 Simeonof Earthquake from July 2020. It was widely felt throughout the Aleutian Islands, the Alaskan Peninsula, and the Cook Inlet regions. A tsunami warning was issued for the Alaska Peninsula and Kodiak Island, prompting evacuations in some coastal communities. The warning was later downgraded to an advisory and then canceled. The highest recorded tsunami waves were half a foot in King Cove and Sand Point, and no damage was reported. The earthquake's epicenter was approximately 60-66 miles south of Sand Point. The event was the result of thrust faulting on the subduction zone interface between the Pacific and North American plates.

While a small tsunami of about 0.2 feet was measured at Sand Point, no significant tsunami was observed, and the initial warning was later downgraded to an advisory before being canceled. There were no initial reports of significant damage from the earthquake or the small tsunami it generated. Seismologists consider this earthquake to be part of the prolonged aftershock sequence of the magnitude 7.8 Simeonof earthquake that occurred in the same region in July 2020. <10> An earthquake swarm, confirmed as the largest ever recorded at Mount Rainier, began at 1:29 a.m. PDT on July 8, 2025. [5, 7] The swarm consisted of over a thousand small earthquakes, with the number of located events exceeding 1,100 by the end of the month. [4, 8] The largest tremor, a magnitude 2.4, was recorded at 12:23 p.m. PDT on July 11, 2025. [5, 6, 9] Scientists from the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and the Pacific Northwest Seismic Network attributed the swarm to the movement of hydrothermal fluids through existing faults deep beneath the volcano, not to the movement of magma. [4, 9] Consequently, the activity was not considered a sign of impending eruption, and the volcano's alert level remained at GREEN / NORMAL. [5, 6, 9, 10, 11] While the rate of earthquakes peaked on July 8, with as many as 41 located events per hour, it decreased significantly in the following days and weeks. [5, 6]
